title: reduce-cpu-contention-in-request-path-thread-pinning-and-serialization
author: Samir Patel
description: Motivation: Production load tests showed periodic tail-latency spikes for small requests (<64 tokens) under mixed workload. Investigation pointed to CPU-side contention in the request path: expensive JSON serialization on the main request threads, suboptimal thread-pool scheduling, and collisions on KV-cache metadata locks when continuous batching and kernel scheduling are active. This PR reduces CPU contention by: 1) introducing a fast-path serializer for compact responses (avoid full JSON marshalling for simple response shapes), 2) separating IO/serialization from compute worker pools and adding explicit thread pinning/affinity policies for compute-heavy worker threads, 3) making KV-cache metadata updates lock-free for the common hit-path (atomic reference updates + epoch counter) and adding per-shard locks for misses, and 4) improving the continuous-batching scheduler to pre-warm KV cache and prefer co-located requests to reduce cache thrashing. Checklist: - [x] microbenchmarks for serializer fast-path - [x] end-to-end perf tests (local and perf lab) - [x] unit tests for lock-free KV metadata path - [x] feature-flag gated rollout - [x] documentation update in runtime/README Highlights: - Serializer fast-path reduces CPU cycles on small responses by ~55% (measured via flamegraphs). Implementation inserts a lightweight path that formats tokens and metadata into a preallocated buffer when response shape is one of {text, single-choice, short-structured}. - Thread re-architecture: request-acceptor threads now offload response serialization and network writes to a dedicated IO pool. Compute workers (model forward/KV handling) are pinned to a configured set of cores using a new runtime config option cpu.affinity.compute_cores. This isolates NUMA-local compute from background IO and GC noise. - KV-cache: common hit path now performs an atomic pointer read and epoch check (no mutex). Miss path uses per-shard spinlocks and background revalidation to avoid holding locks during model execution. - Batching scheduler heuristics: when affinity is enabled, the scheduler batches requests with similar model variant and origin region to improve KV-cache locality and kernel codepath reuse. Commits (summary): - add fast-path serializer and benchmarks - introduce IO worker pool and cpu.affinity config - implement lock-free KV metadata read and per-shard locks for misses - update continuous-batcher to pass affinity hints - tests + perf harness updates Files changed (high level): - runtime/serialize/fast_serializer.rs (new) - runtime/serialize/mod.rs (fast-path integration) - runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.rs (heuristics) - runtime/kv_cache/shard.rs (per-shard locks + lock-free read) - runtime/config.rs (cpu.affinity options) - integration_tests/perf/cpu_contention.yaml - docs/runtime/affinity.md Performance results: On perf-lab medium cluster (8 CPU-core workers, synthetic mixed load with 30% small responses) we see: - median latency: -8% - p95 latency: -24% - CPU user-time per-request: -33% - token throughput (stable): +5% Locking down rollout: change gated behind feature flag runtime.flags.cpu_contention_mitigation; default off for 1 week, canary to 10% of traffic for customers on dedicated. Migration notes: configuration cpu.affinity.compute_cores accepts comma-separated core lists; defaults to empty (disabled). This change is backwards compatible and controlled by the feature flag. Related: ENG-5472 (profiling), ENG-5500 (kv-cache regressions).

review_comments: Maya Rivera (reviewer): Can you add a fallback to the full serializer if the fast-path buffer overflows? Concerned about edge-case response shapes.
Samir Patel (author): Added a bounded check and fallback; updated bench to include overflow case. See commit a1b2c3d.
Ethan Cole (reviewer): The thread pinning looks good, but please add a startup validation that configured cores exist on the host to avoid invalid affinity masks.
Samir Patel (author): Added validation and clearer error messages; tests for invalid masks included.
Priya Nandakumar (approver): Verified p95 improvements on perf-lab. Approving, please ensure feature-flag rollout plan is followed.

ci_checks: Integration perf tests: flaky -> rerun -> pass
release_notes: Reduce CPU-side contention in request path: serializer fast-path, thread affinity for compute workers, lock-free KV-cache read path, and improved batching heuristics. Feature-flag gated rollout.
notes: This PR targets production runtime performance and should be monitored closely during the canary. Metric owners: @infra-perf, alert on p95 regression > 15% for small-response workload.
